source: All sheets, column C "Raw data/Data set/Product name"
coding_and_derivation: Kept as given, except where a provider has supplied a clearer name. Rows carrying the same name, provider and input are merged into one product; the hazards and dissemination routes are collected on that product.

Mapped to the six data-call hazards by keyword. "Tropical Cyclones (multi-hazards: wind…", "Tropical cyclones", "FIRE", "Drought" and "Volcanic Ash" are folded into single labels. One cell listing four hazards yields four hazard tags. "Heavy Rain, Flooding monitoring" is read as Floods.
Verbatim, with SAF names spaced (EUMETSAT LSA SAF) and the two spellings of the Russian centre merged.
Ten operator families. The SWCEM sheet is a WMO programme rather than an operator: its rows are attributed to JAXA and NOAA as stated in the provider column, and tagged "WMO SWCEM".

Pattern-matched to 27 satellite or platform families. Non-satellite inputs — ground and in-situ networks, model and reanalysis fields — are held under one label, "Ground, in-situ and model inputs", so blended products are not read as pure satellite products. The verbatim cell is shown on the product.

source: Derived from product name and stated purpose
coding_and_derivation: Thirteen groups derived from what the sheets actually contain, not an imposed taxonomy. Products whose name matches more than one group are placed by name first, purpose second.
Seven classes. "Full disk" is resolved by operator: East Asia & Western Pacific for KMA and CMA, Indian Ocean & South Asia for IMD and ISRO. Verbatim extent is shown on the product.

Read from the data-policy column: free/open; free/open with conditions on some routes (where a product is open on one route but needs NMHS credentials or covers delivery cost on another, as with the JMA Himawari routes); free with NMHS credentials required; provider data-policy terms (EUMETSAT and JAXA policy links, Copernicus terms); not stated. Every verbatim policy statement is shown on the product, so a mixed case can be read route by route.
Four classes from 15 source variants: Operational (includes "Released", "routine production", "Standard product"); pre-operational or in development; research product; demonstration.
Near real-time / delayed mode / both / not stated, from 18 source variants. The verbatim value is kept on the product.

source: Column K "Dissemination mechanism(s)" with column L "URL(s)"
coding_and_derivation: One route per distinct dissemination-and-URL pair. This is what collapses the 15 JMA Himawari imagery rows into one product with five routes (HimawariCast, HimawariCloud, WIS GISC Tokyo, JDDS, JMBSC).
Values written entirely in capitals (HALF HOURLY, THREE HOURLY, DAILY; FULL DISK; INDIAN REGION) are set in sentence case. Acronyms, satellite names, formats and units keep their case.

source: Column R "Training Resources" plus the Australian VLab CoE document
coding_and_derivation: Held once each at hazard level with operator and satellite cross-references, never repeated per product.

Normalised to "start – end", with "present" for an open archive and the most precise start the provider gave (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). Excel date serials on the EUMETSAT sheet were converted to dates; "since 1998", "Since November 2022" and KMA’s "2019.7.25. ~" were rewritten to the same pattern; multi-satellite and multi-component answers keep each component with its own period in brackets. Three answers stated a retention period ("3 days", "1 day", "12 hours") rather than a start date; these are shown as not stated, with the original kept in the dataset.
A blank cell is shown as "Not stated" and never counted as a negative. An explicit "N/A", "-" or "n.a." is shown as "None / not applicable". The two are distinguished everywhere.
